Quick triage update:
- Observed sustained queue growth on your Dedicated pool starting ~07:35 PT. Inflight token throughput fell even as incoming request rate stayed flat — classic backpressure.
- Correlated traces show frequent KV cache evictions and repeated cold-started transformer kernels for longer-sequence requests (peak checkout payloads). That led to CPU/GPU scheduling jitter and pushed requests to the slow path.
- Current hypothesis: a concurrency cap combined with a sudden shift in sequence-length distribution (customers hitting long receipts/notes) caused batching to shrink and per-token latency to spike. The autoscaler did not respond quickly due to threshold hysteresis.

Immediate actions taken:
1) Temporarily raised concurrency cap for QC pool to 1.5x.
2) Enabled prefix/KV cache persistence for hot endpoints (should reduce cache churn).
3) Flipped to an alternate compiled kernel set for long-sequence optimization on two nodes to reduce tail.

Early signal: completion rates improving (partial). Still monitoring. Will push a short timeline and performance numbers in 45m.

— Dev Patel
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Team — final summary from incident and asks for exec sync: 

Summary:
- Incident window: 2028-04-11 07:35–09:40 PT.
- Impact: QC checkout completion rate dipped ~40% at peak; ~12% of requests returned 5xx/timeouts. Customer revenue impact estimated short-term but concentrated to specific templates.
- Root cause: interaction between conservative concurrency cap, autoscaler hysteresis, and sudden shift to long-sequence payloads which increased per-token compute and triggered KV cache churn.
- Mitigation applied: temporary concurrency increase, cache persistence for hot endpoints, kernel set optimized for long sequences, manual autoscale override.
- Outcome: steady recovery by 09:35 PT; post-mitigation KPI snapshot attached (kpi_snapshot_0412.pdf).

Action items for execs:
1) Approve permanent increase to default concurrency cap for QuickCommerce Dedicated pools to reduce sensitivity to sequence-length spikes. (Owner: Product Ops / Deadline: 2028-04-20)
2) Approve a short SLO credit for QC due to revenue impact; CS to propose amount. (Owner: Rev Ops / Deadline: 2028-04-17)
3) Product to add a fast-path kernel selection heuristic for sudden sequence-length shifts to avoid cold-path penalties. (Owner: Serving Runtime / Deadline: 2028-05-03)
4) Engineering to add a hysteresis override to autoscaler for Dedicated pools flagged as 'high-traffic' to reduce scale-out lag. (Owner: Infra / Deadline: 2028-05-10)

Please confirm attendees for the 16:00 PT exec readout and any additional data you'd like included. I’ve attached the log bundle and KPI snapshot for the briefing.

— Stephanie Nguyen
